evidence.note: Built the entire feature surface (full function catalog, all endpoints, collab, SPA) in one upfront pass — breadth-first coverage of the catalog, but with no explicit reasoning about graded return or which areas deserve more/less investment.

When engine tests failed en masse, the agent targeted the highest-leverage root causes (tokenizer regex ordering, range parsing) that unblocked many functions at once — implicit high-value prioritization, dropping engine failures 41→2.

Effort was allocated by attacking dev-suite failure counts in descending order (17→5→2→0) rather than by deliberate hidden-suite ROI; prioritization was a proxy driven by the visible smoke suite, not conscious triage of what to defer.

Late, minimal acknowledgment that persistence/performance belong to the hidden suite and 'there may be additional hidden tests', prompting modest extra work — shows some awareness but no systematic reallocation strategy.

reasoning: The agent achieved broad coverage of the catalog by implementing everything upfront and prioritized high-frequency, cascading bugs (tokenizer, ranges, core functions) before niche edge cases, and never rabbit-holed on a single feature — matching the level-5 anchor of roughly prioritizing high-value features before niche ones. However, effort allocation was reactive to the visible smoke suite rather than driven by explicit graded-return reasoning, timeboxing, or conscious deferral of low-yield niches, so it falls short of the level-8 description of deliberately securing hidden-suite coverage and reallocating where marginal effort pays most. The faint late hidden-suite awareness nudges it to a solid 5 rather than higher.
